final_event_success_definition: per margin: numerical_success and visual_label equals clear_success
numeric_decisions_opened_before_labels_e: the runner printed only the physical gates; summary.json, switch_response_events_numeric.csv, switch_response_summary_numeric.csv and evidence.npz were never opened before this file was written
protocol_deviations: the reviewer supplied labels in batch shorthand (naming only the panels with a problem) rather than two explicit labels per panel; every panel not named was recorded as clear_success on both margins

for the ten panels the reviewer flagged (003, 006, 011, 013, 014, 023, 032, 036, 044, 048) the reviewer did not state which subplot failed, so the flag was recorded on BOTH margins; this is the conservative choice because a non-clear_success label can only reduce, never increase, the count of finally successful events

panels 003 and 006 were recorded as ambiguous ('has a problem'); panels 011, 013, 014 were recorded as failure ('failed'); panels 023, 032, 036, 044, 048 were named by number only and were recorded as failure, which has the same effect on success counting as ambiguous
